static_traits.name: Jiang Na
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness;not yet received treatment or counseling for other psychological problems

basic_info.main_problem: I have a tendency to overeat candy during Halloween, which makes me feel guilty and regretful. This behavior started in childhood but became more pronounced in recent years. Despite knowing it is not healthy, I still consume large amounts of candy during Halloween and find it hard to control.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize this behavior is negatively affecting my physical health and overall well-being, so I came to seek counseling; I hope to achieve moderation and balance while enjoying Halloween, reducing guilt and the sense of losing control.
growth_experiences: In childhood, the excitement about Halloween began to form the habit and pattern of eating candy to excess, and afterward, every Halloween, eating that was difficult to control appeared; in the last few years this problem has become more pronounced.

core_beliefs: I lack self-control (I cannot control myself)
Eating candy is wrong; enjoyment equals unhealthiness

special_situations.event: During Halloween, the home and surroundings are filled with lots of candy and a festive atmosphere
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once I start eating, I will definitely lose control; if I lose control it proves I lack self-control
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Before festivals, sets strict limits and self-control rules for oneself, trying to suppress cravings with willpower
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I definitely will not be able to stop; in the end I will still overeat

special_situations.event: After starting to eat a few candies, shifts from enjoyment to self-judgment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I eat candy, it is unhealthy and it is wrong
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses self-blame and guilt to restrain oneself, trying to use guilt to stop continued eating
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not eat this; it is very unhealthy

special_situations.event: Strong guilt and regret upon realizing one has eaten too much
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once the rule is broken it counts as total failure; since I failed, there is no need for restraint anymore
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Simply keeps eating to temporarily numb guilt (emotional eating)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Anyway I have already eaten too much, might as well finish them all

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be allowed to enjoy beloved things without guilt, and to be understood and accepted in close relationships
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing control, harming health, and thereby affecting the relationship with daughters, triggering shame and guilt
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control through strict 'should/should not' self-Demands
Avoiding discussing this trouble with daughters so as not to make them 'carry a burden'

object_relations.self_representation: A self who feels guilty, easily loses control, and needs to be restrained
object_relations.object_representation: Daughters are people who may be troubled or affected by me; I need to restrain myself to not bother them

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests communicating this trouble with daughters or exploring the relational level
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I say it, it will burden them and make me look very embarrassed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'not wanting to trouble them' in a hesitant and apologetic tone, downplaying deep emotions, shifting focus to concrete strategies.

manifestations: Limiting oneself with internalized 'should/should not' rules
Worrying that relaxing will lead to losing control
outcomes: Tension in the relationship with daughters
Daily self-care and eating rhythms affected

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly using 'should/should not' self-judgment (like 'I should not eat candy')
Taking the creed 'health = absolutely no candy' as the only standard

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Intense self-blame after guilt, tightening self-restraint
Reluctant to seek help for fear of burdening daughters

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not communicating the trouble with daughters and choosing to bear it alone
Handles guilt emotions through self-blame and further eating

positive_force: Clear motivation; proactively seeks help because health and well-being are affected
Positive attitude, willing to try mindfulness and cognitive restructuring
Able to notice the cycle pattern of 'enjoyment - guilt - continued eating'
Having potential support resources (living with daughters, can communicate)
negative_force: The belief 'I cannot control myself' leading to anticipatory loss of control
Shame and embarrassment blocking seeking support from family
Repeatedly triggering problems in high-cue situations of festivals and large amounts of candy

antecedent: The Halloween festive atmosphere and excitement
Large amounts of candy easily available at home and around
After eating a few pieces, enjoyment turns into self-blame
target_behavior.core_reason: Strong love of candy combined with festival excitement; briefly regulating guilt by continuing to eat; negative beliefs about self-control and rigid rules triggering rebound
target_behavior.function: Gaining immediate pleasure and brief relief from negative emotions (Guilt, stress)
target_behavior.consequence: Physical health and self-care affected; guilt and regret persist; tension in the relationship with daughters
